Hi Alice — Marcus here. Below is a concise, customer-facing summary addressing your bullets. I've attached the detailed subprocessor matrix and an annotated KMS diagram to the shared Drive link in the header.

1) Subprocessors (short list):
- Cloud Provider: Redwood Cloud Infra (us-west-2) — hosts containerized inference runtime; access limited to orchestration for tenant isolation; no plaintext model input access (encrypted at rest).
- Model repo & optimizer vendor: ModelOpsInc — transient build artifacts only; no access to production request logs.
- Logging/Observability: LogStreamCo — stores aggregated token-level metrics and anonymized traces; full request payloads are redacted by default.
- Vector indexing service: VecStore LLC — stores embeddings (hashed); keys are customer-scoped when Dedicated or Private.

2) Access statements (who can see PII):
- By default (hosted), request inputs/outputs are retained encrypted and only accessible via limited support tooling with recorded approvals. Subprocessors do not have direct access to unredacted PII in production unless explicitly enabled for a troubleshooting session and scoped by support SOPs.

3) Retention windows (default hosted):
- Request logs (metadata only): 30 days
- Model inputs/outputs (full): 90 days (default) — can be shortened or configured for Dedicated/Private customers
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, caches): 180 days for hosted; customer-managed for Dedicated/Private

4) KMS handling (summary):
- Hosted customers: keys managed by Redwood KMS; keys rotate annually; export not permitted.
- Dedicated: customer KMS integration via customer-managed keys (CMK) — we support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) with rotation policies.
- Private/on-prem: full custody by customer; Redwood provides integration playbooks.

5) Incident notification & attestation:
- Privacy-impacting incidents: 72-hour initial notification SLA, 30-day remediation timeline with periodic updates.
- Proof points available: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), KMS attestation statement, and a sample redacted breadcrumb log.

Attachments we pushed to Drive (shared link above):
- redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v1.xlsx (contains subprocessors, region, purpose, access level)
- redwood_kms_key_access_annotated.pdf (diagram + custodian roles)
- access_breadcrumbs_sample.log (redacted sample)

Open items / asks:
- Beacon: confirm whether you require a shorter retention baseline for model inputs (e.g., 30 days) and whether we should include a separate DPA addendum for BYOK contracts.
- Beacon: please confirm HubSpot deal id/match (we captured DEAL-8472) and whether legal should loop in procurement now.

I'll be available on Tuesday afternoon to jump on a quick call if you want to walk the artifacts together.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Staff Security Engineer, Privacy Controls | Redwood Inference
